bull.b: Consistent operating and free cash flow provides durable funding for unit growth, HEEP rollout, and buybacks without needing external capital. Strong cash conversion supports reinvestment in throughput, loyalty and return of capital while cushioning cyclical revenue swings.

bull.t: High digital penetration and HEEP throughput
bull.b: A large, growing digital mix plus HEEP equipment that materially raises peak throughput are structural advantages: lower per-order labor, higher attach rates and better order accuracy sustain margins and frequency, making revenue growth less reliant on traffic alone.

bull.t: Rapid unit expansion with solid unit economics
bull.b: Aggressive openings, especially Chipotlanes, scale a proven concept with attractive year-2 cash-on-cash returns. Stable new-unit productivity and drive-thru convenience diversify formats and underpin multi-year revenue growth and incremental operating leverage as the portfolio matures.

bear.b: Meaningful margin erosion from higher food, freight and labor costs is a sustained threat to unit economics. Unless offset by permanent pricing, productivity gains, or scale-driven cost declines, compressed margins can reduce free cash flow and constrain long-term reinvestment.

Higher debt levels reduce balance-sheet flexibility for funding openings, weathering downturns, or pursuing opportunistic M&A. Even with improvement, elevated leverage increases interest exposure and constrains the company’s ability to scale capex and aggressive buybacks simultaneously.

A persistent gap in in-store rewards adoption limits customer data capture and targeted marketing, reducing lifetime value extraction from dine-in traffic. Structural friction in enrollment impedes loyalty-driven frequency gains and weakens personalization-driven margin upside.
